responsibility: Implements the main C-side target backend for AMD GCN, supplying the port’s target hooks, ABI logic, builtin handling, register and mode legality rules, calling convention, addressing and constant classification, frame and trampoline support, costs, DWARF/debug mappings, vectorization preferences, OpenMP/OpenACC integration, and kernel metadata/attribute handling. It owns per-function machine state such as LDS allocations and reduction temporaries, derives ISA and option-dependent defaults like PIE and stack size, and binds all of this behavior into GCC through the TARGET_INITIALIZER hook table for the GCN machine description.
same_name_distinction: This is the executable C-side backend implementation for the GCN port: unlike gcn.h it defines the target-hook functions and per-function state machinery that use the header’s macros and data structures, unlike gcn.md it does not encode instruction selection as RTL patterns, and unlike gcn.opt it consumes the generated target-option variables rather than declaring the command-line options themselves.
